sources.citation: Laufer, Berthold. 1919. Sino-Iranica: Chinese contributions to the history of civilization in ancient Iran, with special reference to the history of cultivated plants and products. Field Museum of Natural History Publ. 201, Anthropological Series 15(3), pp. 185-630. Chicago. Appendix 'The Malayan Po-se and Its Products', pp. 468-487; language material pp. 472-474.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The entire linguistic attestation is (pp. 472-473) a list of numerals 1-10, 20, 30, 40, 100, 1000 in Japanese kana transcription from the Kōdanshō ('Memoirs of Ōe', early 12th c.) as reported by Tsuboi Kumazō 1899 and identified as Malayan by Florenz (e.g. 1 sasaa/sasaka, 2 toa, 5 rima, 10 sararo, 100 sasarato), plus two words in Chinese transcription from the Youyang zazu (pai-han 'ivory', hei-han 'rhinoceros horn'). Laufer: 'However meagre the linguistic material may be, it reveals, at any rate, Malayan affinities'. No phonology, no accent.
